previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of kidney transplant, coronary artery disease, and multiple comorbidities, was admitted for acute substernal chest pain radiating to the left neck and arm. Workup revealed negative troponins and no EKG changes, ruling out acute coronary syndrome. The pain was determined to be angina due to known CAD, particularly involving the LCx territory with occluded obtuse marginal arteries. Management included uptitrating amlodipine from 5 to 10 mg daily, continuing beta-blocker and antiplatelet therapy, and advising nitroglycerin use as needed. She also had acute on chronic kidney injury with admission creatinine of 2.7, likely prerenal, which improved to 2.1 with IV fluids. Transplant function was stable, with tacrolimus levels adjusted to therapeutic range. She remained asymptomatic during admission and was discharged home with follow-up planned with cardiology and nephrology.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ woman with a history of FSGN s/p 
renal transplant in ___, DVT/PE (previously on Coumadin but 
stopped due to hemarthrosis), CAD, anemia, s/p prior breast 
reduction surgery and now s/p breast fat necrosis removal on 
___ who presents with confusion and acute on chronic renal 
disease.  

#Confusion: Her confusion appeared to start after her scheduled 
outpatient surgery, with symptoms described as feeling ""fuzzy"" 
and ""slow"" starting ___. Differential included infection, 
medication effect, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy, and CVA. 
Given positive opioids in urine, and patient taking dilaudid for 
post-op pain but being opioid naive, this seemed most likely 
opioid related effect. On exam, patient was drowsy but oriented 
and able to follow commands, which improved on its own during 
her course. Her repeat urine tox was positive for opiates and 
pupils were pinpoint, also suggesting medication effect. 
Infectious work-up was negative to date and there was no 
evidence of wound infection. She had complained of neck 
stiffness, and thus an LP was attempted but was technically 
difficult and unable to be completed. Her neck stiffness 
improved with pain control, with no new neurological symptoms. 

# Acute on chronic renal disease: Cr on admission was 3.7, up 
from most recent baseline of 2.0, improved to her baseline with 
fluids. Given her recent feeling dehydrated, prerenal was the 
most likely etiology.  Urine protein/Cr normal. Her home lasix 
was held. It was unclear whether patient had taken Lasix 80 mg 
instead of 40 mg at home, she was instructed to take lasix 40.

# Acute on chronic anemia: Patient had a baseline anemia with 
most recent baseline Hg around ___. Iron studies last month 
were consistent with anemia of chronic disease/CKD. Hg on 
admission was 8.6. There were signs of active bleeding though 
patient had a recent major surgery, which was the most likely 
etiology of this acute anemia, with no signs of hemolysis. Her 
labs remained stable during her course.

#History of FSGN s/p renal transplant: Continued Sirolimus 2 mg 
PO DAILY and Tacrolimus 2 mg PO QAM, Tacrolimus 1 mg PO QPM.

# Hypertension: Patient's pressures appeared to be lower than 
usual, no infectious etiology as above, thus amlodipine was 
decreased from 10 mg to 5 mg, also as patient had reported 
worsening leg swelling, for which she had taken a higher lasix 
dose.
